quest.title: A Space and Time Without You
quest.description: Many strange events have unfolded between you and the girl named Direidyth, all while the conflict between the Abyss Order and Natlan rages on. Amidst this turmoil, the one who will shift the tides of war is preparing to take the stage...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1125, Primogem x60, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

chapter.title: A Space and Time for You

talks.objective: Meet up at the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Iansan, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We ran into quite a big group from the Abyss Order just now. Has something happened at the front?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The front line has collapsed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? But how!?

choices.text: Did the Abyss Order send in reinforcements?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: No, no, relax. THEIR front line has collapsed, not ours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... Feels like you could've phrased that more clearly at the start... This is good news, right? Why do you still look so serious?

choices.text: Did we finally launch an attack?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: No... We're still mustering troops. Nowhere near ready to go on the offensive.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: So at first, I was also confused about what exactly happened out there...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: But just now, I got the full story from a guard who was on the scene. He watched the enemy lines crumble in real time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What did he see?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: ...One person. Just a single individual... They stormed the enemy lines and attacked with a vengeance, cutting them down like paper dolls...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: They wielded an unknown power, and fought with a sword style that no one recognized... The guard who relayed this to me said that before he even had time to react, the enemy was decimated...

choices.text: Alright, I got it...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I'm only recounting what I heard, and I'm sure the guard in question must be exaggerating to some extent... But still, we have to identify this person...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: And assuming they're a neutral party, we'll need to figure out how to engage with them... Clearly, they're a force to be reckoned with, so we don't want to come across as too weak or too hostile... It's quite a diplomatic conundrum.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... You don't need to sweat it, Iansan. From your description we're already pretty confident that we know this person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Honestly, with the Abyss Order acting out so publicly, it's about time he showed up...

choices.text: Yeah. Who else could it be?

response.speaker: #{NICKNAME} & Paimon
response.text: ...Dainsleif!

choices.text: He never misses an occasion like this...
I think I know what happened...
Did we unleash the Pyro Archon's might on them?
Did they deploy some kind of secret weapon?

talks.objective: Wait for Dainsleif to show up

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hmm? Were you... waiting for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Dain! And yeah, after we heard what went down, we figured you'd shown up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You caused quite a stir, you know. Um... this is a friend of ours from Natlan. Her name's Iansan. She insisted on coming here to thank you in person.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It is my honor, Mr. Dainsleif.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Thank you for breaking the stalemate in our war against the Abyss Order. Natlan is fortunate to share a common enemy with such a mighty warrior as yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: No need to thank me. I hunt the Abyss Order for my own reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Please don't mind him, Iansan! He always talks like that, but he's a pretty nice guy deep down.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It's quite alright. Uwe{RUBY#[S]Power}zo Iansan respects those of great power. It's quite clear that he meant no offense, and I am still delighted to make his acquaintance.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Anyway, since you're old friends, I'll leave you to catch up for now. Take your time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing. You probably have plenty of other stuff to do anyway, right? Since this war isn't exactly over. See ya later, Iansan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Dain, would it have killed you to be a little more polite? She's our friend!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Iansan, yes? I will remember the name. But I will not invest more emotion than is necessary when dealing with the citizens of The Seven. It is a matter of principle for me.

choices.text: Fine. Since you helped break the stalemate, we'll let you off the hook.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, so stubborn... but whatever. So anyway, Dain, do you have any new info about the Abyss Order for us? Any idea what they're trying to achieve with this war, for example?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Never before have I seen the Abyss Order take action on such a large scale...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Taken at face value, it seems highly illogical. In a war with the Natlanese, the odds are stacked firmly against them — they surely cannot be unaware of this. Their true goal must be a deeper one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We thought so too! But it sounds like you're no closer to learning what that goal is than we are.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I've been on the case for some time. Even captured and interrogated several Abyss Order members...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Yet still, I am none the wiser. I can only assume they have gone to great lengths to keep their real operations a secret.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I have a bad feeling about this. The Abyss Order is wasting a lot of its forces attacking Natlan, so whatever they stand to gain must hold enormous value to them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you think we should do?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Since we lack actionable intelligence, for now, we might as well continue to focus on the fighting.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Leave them to their secret plots. If they're so willing to sacrifice manpower for it, I intend to make that sacrifice greater and more painful than they could ever have anticipated.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: If we use this opportunity correctly, I believe we can eliminate the vast majority of the Abyss Order's forces.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: They'll never be able to mount such a large campaign ever again. That outcome is well worth our time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And the sooner we can do that, the better.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That's right. The ideal scenario would be to destroy them before they can reach their goal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it: Nothing in the world can satisfy you like making mincemeat out of the Abyss Order, right?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, okay... A rare candid response from Dain...

choices.text: Sounds like Dain's one-man attack on the enemy front...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: What about you? Any news to share from your end?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, actually... We found {M#his sister}{F#her brother}'s Hibernation Chamber key near the Collective of Plenty. {M#She}{F#He} must've lost it...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #So {M#she}{F#he}'s here in person... Unsurprising, given the scale of this operation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and there's more! After finding the key, we also ran into this weird girl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She kept seeing monsters that we couldn't see... And then, this other time, we saw a load of monsters, but she couldn't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #She also said she was on a journey to find the "Savior." Her description of this savior matched {NICKNAME} pretty closely, so we figured it's probably {M#his sister}{F#her brother}...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #Hold on... That girl called {M#her}{F#him} the Savior?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's right! Is something the matter, Dain?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #The last time I heard that term was before the Cataclysm... And not just that — it referred to your {M#sister}{F#brother} then, too.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: But who would still believe in the myth of the Savior when the Cataclysm has already taken place...? It makes no sense.

choices.text: That term's been around...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, wasn't {M#his sister}{F#her brother} called the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} though? Where did this Savior thing come from?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #Well, when {M#she}{F#he} was first granted the title of {M#Princess}{F#Prince}...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #The Vinster King and the entire Court of Khaenri'ah set about loudly proclaiming the might that {M#she}{F#he} would bring to the nation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #They made it sound as if with {M#her}{F#him} there, all pain and suffering would be washed away, and the future of Khaenri'ah would be brighter than anyone could imagine...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #"The Savior" was the celebratory title given to the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} by those who believed this rhetoric.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Of course, you know how that story ended. In hindsight, the cruel irony is glaring. All that title really stood for was the Vinster King's lust for power.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sounds like the people of Khaenri'ah really believed in {M#her}{F#him}...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(Is that why {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} is so determined to revive the homeland? Because {M#she}{F#he} thinks {M#she's}{F#he's} failed as the Khaenri'ahn's Savior?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But that certainly doesn't explain everything. There must be other reasons.)

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: As for the girl you met... Allow me to offer some speculation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I suspect she is descended from pure-blood Khaenri'ahns afflicted with the curse of immortality. They must have re-settled somewhere remote, cut off from the rest of the world.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That would explain how her people retained their ancient beliefs, including the myth of the golden-haired Savior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Paimon gets it now! So, a bit like Kaeya? Except she grew up somewhere more isolated?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, that doesn't explain the invisible monster situation...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: If she can't provide us with any more valuable intelligence, I suggest we shift our attention back to the Abyss Order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure. Also, why don't you stay with us at the Masters of the Night-Wind for tonight? You must be tired after all that fighting today.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I will consider it, but we must discuss our next steps first thing tomorrow morning. We can't give the Abyss Order any time to regroup.

choices.text: Even before the Cataclysm?
...Has put him in a good mood.
Fine... Since Iansan wasn't offended, we'll let you off the hook.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...No, we can't give them that much time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that... Dain and Iansan discussing strategy together? Huh, looks like they're getting along just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning! What are you guys talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. I have some good news to share with you.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We just got word from the Scions of the Canopy. Their intelligence has reported that they've discovered the Abyss Order's headquarters in Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: After their front lines dissolved, the bulk of their forces fell back to that area. It's also where their central command is located.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The location — the Cinder City.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cinder City, huh? That tracks... seems like their kind of place. Hey, this is great! This could be our chance to crush the Abyss Order once and for all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And with any luck, maybe we'll find your {M#sister}{F#brother} there, too!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yep. Our army is almost ready, and we've sent a message to Mavuika to let her know the plan. We can't really launch an operation this big without the okay from the Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I beg to differ. This is wasting time.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: You have the intel you need, so act on it. Every second you delay only increases the Abyss Order's odds of survival.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I've already explained my reasoning, Mr. Dainsleif. I understand your concern, but an immediate strike is not on the cards for us.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Very well, then I will go there alone. Thank you for the intel, Iansan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're gonna go on your own!? Come on, be sensible. Just wait a tiny bit longer, and you'll have a whole army going with you...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It's all right. I support your decision, Mr. Dainsleif.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Shouldn't you be talking sense into him?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I admire his courage, and I believe he is strong enough to take on the Abyss Order on his own.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: And even if things don't go to plan, he just needs to bide his time until we arrive with reinforcements.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Mr. Dainsleif... I wish you the very best of luck.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Mm, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... Looks like he's waiting for you to say something, {NICKNAME}...

choices.text: Allow me to join you, Dainsleif.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh*... For a second there, Paimon actually thought he was gonna brave it alone... and then he called his own bluff.

choices.text: Alright, fine, I'm coming...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the place? The Abyss Order's hideout in Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: All these years, the Abyss Order has managed to either stay hidden or fiercely defend their position... This may be the first chance I've ever had to finally make a serious dent in their forces.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Which reminds me — once the fighting starts, I can't promise I'll be able to have your back at a moment's notice...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: But if you run into any Abyss-powered mechanisms, feel free to leave them to me. I'll take care of them when I can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been so long since we fought with Dain side-by-side. Paimon's confident we can clear this place out long before Iansan arrives!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And if you get to meet your {M#sister}{F#brother} again, even better. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: So that's what happened... Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, must have had a hand in this.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: There's no other way that this meeting could have taken place.

choices.text: #{M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I knew only the ending. I've always been curious about the events that led to it.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: #When the Cataclysm first began five hundred years ago, I, as the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} of Khaenri'ah, was preparing to do my part — to fight back with all my might...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: But then this girl, Direidyth... she found me.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: The irony was that even as she desperately begged me to save the world... she brought me news of you.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I was stunned. And I was suspicious of her claim that you were searching for me... But then, she showed me the key to your Hibernation Chamber.

choices.text: So...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: We'd been separated ever since I awakened in Teyvat. I searched the whole planet, and found no trace of you anywhere... And then she brought me that news at the worst possible moment...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I was faced with an extremely difficult decision.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I desperately wanted to see you again. But Khaenri'ah was in equally desperate need of my help.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I knew that no matter what I chose, I'd regret my decision for the rest of my days.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: So I steeled myself against the guilt and made my decision. I went to see you.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: But when I found you, you were still in hibernation. Even the key to the chamber was still secure on your person.

choices.text: You're saying...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I couldn't make sense of what I was seeing, but there was no time to think... I just grabbed you and ran. That's where we are right now — an intersection in our memories.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: This question has haunted me for the past five hundred years... I never imagined the answer would come to me like this.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: So, my actions five hundred years in the future set everything in motion... Are you mocking me, Istaroth?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Direidyth succeeded in bringing us together. But unfortunately, it is versions of us five hundred years apart.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She hoped that the Savior would rescue Khaenri'ah, save the entire world... but instead, the news she brought led the Savior to make the complete opposite decision...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (How awful... Is that her fate? Is that how her story must end?)

choices.text: Has Khaenri'ah really been revived?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Not yet, but I've taken a very important step. Now, the Ley Lines of Khaenri'ah are complete.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I'd always thought that Teyvat's Ley Lines were locked by the Heavenly Principles. No more can be added, and existing ones cannot be replaced.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: But then, I learned that Natlan's Night Kingdom appeared to be an exception to the rule... It has intrigued me ever since.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: So, I directed the Abyss Order to feign an attack on Natlan, buying me some time to enter the Night Kingdom and negotiate with the Lord of the Night.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Unfortunately, for other reasons, even the Night Kingdom cannot host any new Ley Lines... The most I could get was some room to carry out the weaving process.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Lord of the Night did say before that even she can only "reconstruct" Natlan's Ley Lines. It's probably for the same reason.)

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Still, I received the Lord of the Night's permission, and activated the Loom of Fate.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Using an Inteyvat as the base, I was able to grow a realm based on the Khaenri'ah of five hundred years ago, superimposing it over present-day Natlan's spacetime.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: That superimposition is what allowed you and Direidyth to cross paths.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(That's what I saw in my dream... {M#She's}{F#He's} not lying about that, at least. But what I don't understand is, why did the Lord of the Night agree to this?)

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: After that, the new Khaenri'ah was enriched with memories of the old, drawn from the Abyss Order's members in their meditation sessions.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: With those memories as raw materials, and the superimposed realm as a template, the Loom of Fate finally finished its work.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: What I now hold in my hand is the Atlas of the New World.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: This is the product of the Loom of Fate, holding within it the entire network of New Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines. With this, the nation once known as Khaenri'ah can rise again.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: One day... I will find a suitable host location for it.

choices.text: Why...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't understand.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: When I first arrived in Khaenri'ah, five hundred years ago... My memory was completely blank.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: #It was only after I had served as their {M#Princess}{F#Prince} for many years that I slowly began to remember everything, including you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What? Your memories were erased!?)

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: But recovering old memories didn't simply erase the part of my life I spent in Khaenri'ah. I still see it as my second home.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: That is why my guilt weighs so heavily on me. But even so, that only constitutes part of my motive.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: More importantly...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: If I wish to speak with the Heavenly Principles as an equal, I will need the might of an entire world behind me.

choices.text: Why is reviving Khaenri'ah so important to you?
Have you done what you set out to do?
Three keys existed simultaneously in that moment?
And then?
She actually did it?
You... knew of all this?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: I know you always want to change fate — we both do. But this time, I won't let you succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: I cannot miss the chance to reunite with you five hundred years in the past — no matter what.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Assuming he is right, then another possibility arises:)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Maybe I'm in a different time and space from Direidyth. If she's Khaenri'ahn like Dain suspects, then that means...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This revived Khaenri'ah that he speaks of might actually exist... And despite hailing from that separate time and space, Direidyth has found a way to communicate with us.)

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Whatever may be going through your mind right now, do not trust it. I urge you not to believe his lies.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The notion that Khaenri'ah has been revived is preposterous. Unless I see it with my own eyes, I refuse to entertain it.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: There is only one thing that should demand our attention in this instant... and that is silencing this man for good!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That should be all of them, right? So... We've destroyed the Abyss Order's headquarters in Natlan, but somehow, that didn't feel satisfying at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Are you still thinking about what that guy said, {NICKNAME}? You look really worried.

choices.text: Direidyth is the only potential lead we have.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I understand. You think... she might be from the revived Khaenri'ah, yes?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I have said my piece — I doubt Khaenri'ah could be revived so easily. But if it will give you some peace of mind, you should talk to her and test your theory.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I will stay here and do some post-battle cleanup. Perhaps there are some clues left to be found.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...Hmph.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I thought your voice and attitude seemed familiar... My mistake. I should have made sure you were dead earlier.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The curse of immortality has struck you too, then, Haden.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Five hundred years on, and you still refuse to address me as "master"...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Don't forget, Dainsleif. You may be the renowned "Twilight Sword," while my arm has grown too feeble to swing a blade...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: ...But I taught you everything you know about wielding a blade.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Hah. Your arrogance and malice cost you all of my respect long ago.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Be that as it may... Under the circumstances, I see no further reason for us to fight. The curse of immortality means neither of us has a way to completely destroy the other.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Speak for yourself. I intend to kill you a hundred times over.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: *panting*

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: *cough*... Have you... finally had enough? You weren't joking then, huh...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Never, in all my worst nightmares, have I experienced anything close to the pain of a hundred deaths... *cough* Surely, there's no point taking out all your hatred on me alone?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: That was just for your actions in the Abyss Order. If I took into account what you did in Khaenri'ah... You'd soon find out how much darker your nightmares can become.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Alright, I believe you. Still, aren't you at least a little tired now? Why don't we sit down, perhaps chat a little?

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: What? Not a fan of reminiscing about old times? Well, I suppose you don't have many fond memories to look back on.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I never thought you'd side with the Abyss Order, Haden.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #You could have easily blamed the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} for {M#her}{F#his} betrayal.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: #Indeed. When the Cataclysm first struck, everyone prayed for the Savior to deliver them, but {M#she}{F#he} was nowhere to be found.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: #Yes, we knew that the great Abyssal power within {M#her}{F#him} had been divided up...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: #Yet we still despaired at {M#her}{F#his} choice to leave us.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: #Still, I believe that everything {M#she's}{F#he's} doing now — including {M#her}{F#his} regret over what happened — comes from a genuine place in {M#her}{F#his} heart.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: And besides, who else can we place our faith in? We are proud Khaenri'ahns, are we not? I mean... we can hardly turn to the gods.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #Hmph. I suppose you have changed a lot over the past five hundred years. Otherwise, I'd have never expected you to forgive {M#her}{F#him}.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Had you been so generous during your time at the Knight Academy as my instructor in Black Serpent Bladework, I might not have come to loathe you so much.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Hehe... Is that so.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: All my good deeds were clearly in the spirit of the Academy's code of chivalry. Yet I received corporal punishment for being "restless and brash."

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: And as much as it pains me to bring up his name... Even my co-student, Surtalogi, was prosecuted for following the spirit of knighthood. He even lost limbs over it.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: There's little point discussing it now, of course, but... All of this was your doing, wasn't it, Haden?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: You wore a mask of benevolence as you viciously suppressed the next generation of knights, all to bolster your own position and reputation.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: What? Too cowardly to admit it?

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: ...I'm sorry, Dainsleif. I would apologize to you for those actions, truly. But the fact is...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: ...I honestly can't remember them anymore.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Look at me — look at what has become of me. Only by the Abyss's grace have I managed to maintain this physical form.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: But as for the rest... Memories, spirit, emotions, personality... They have long become eroded, fragmented beyond recognition.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Even if mine was a past steeped in sin, or in shame I once longed to hide... I would wish to remember it.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Without my history, I... I fear I will become another person entirely.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: ...I would like to apologize for any misdeeds that are mine. So please, tell me everything. Tell me about the Khaenri'ah we once called home.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...No wonder your personality struck me as different. Memories are indeed a crucial part of a person's identity.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: So. The Khaenri'ah we once called home...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Dainsleif slowly closes his eyes. Countless memories of Khaenri'ah flood into his mind...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: All the sights, memories, and feelings — everything etched into the heart and mind — are gradually brought back to the forefront again, alongside a feeling of nostalgia and loss.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Simply recalling everything seems to take a long, long time...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: You seem to remember much... Could you tell me more about it? About our golden age?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I'm not interested. I have neither the time nor the sympathy.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Is that so... What a pity. But this will be quite sufficient, as long as the Loom of Fate heard what I could not...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: The Loom of Fate... What have you done? Tell me.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: I'm afraid I owe you yet another apology, Dainsleif. You were right — I lied to you earlier. Your wits are too sharp to be fooled by me.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: The homeland hasn't yet been revived. In fact, even the Ley Line weaving is not yet complete.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Think of Ley Lines as the collection of memories concerning a given place. To re-weave Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines as they were five hundred years ago, we would somehow need to retrieve almost all the memories of Khaenri'ah from that age.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: The Loom of Fate cannot weave without an abundant supply of memories...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: And so, we relied on everyone in the Abyss Order to provide what they could. Even though fragments are all that remain in most cases, the more we all share, the more that can be restored.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: So, the Loom of Fate is running as we speak? And the so-called "meditation" your members have been performing... its purpose was to supply the Loom with memories, wasn't it?

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Indeed. We, a people in exile, stranded five hundred years in the future, will weave our homeland anew, and bring the nation of our dreams back into the real world. Ah, what a glorious undertaking!

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: What a shame it had to take this long. After five hundred years, most of our memories have faded — and a world woven from broken memories shall itself be broken.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: So that's where I'm supposed to come in? You look for assistance from your mortal enemy, who has sworn to hunt you down?

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Precisely. For you possess a ring, left to you by your elder brother, which continuously resets your body's condition...

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Of course, your memories are susceptible to erosion just like ours. But of all Khaenri'ahns who remain, you are sure to remember the most.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: We had to obtain the memories in your mind, whatever the price. Even if it meant sacrificing our entire army as bait.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...So this was your true goal. To lure me here, guide me into a state of meditation, and access my memories...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: So be it. A few of my fading memories for your entire army? That strikes me as a fair trade. I appreciate your generosity.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: You're gambling everything you have on the Loom of Fate... This could be a costly mistake for you in the long run.

response.speaker: Haden
response.text: Perhaps! But that is the gamble Our Highness has chosen to make. And thanks to you... the Loom of Fate has now finished weaving the Ley Lines. New Khaenri'ah... is complete.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Enough about your beloved leader. You said you would pay any price for my memories, did you not?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: In that case... Prepare to be slain another hundred times for your deception.... I hope it was worth it.

choices.text: I think... we should at least talk to her about all this.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll make sure I find a way to get in touch! Uh, I mean... as long as you don't mind, that is...

talks.objective: Return to the cave to investigate
Head to the Masters of the Night-Wind and talk to Iansan

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Our hero is back! Everyone's been waiting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order made a full retreat before our forces even arrived on the scene... All thanks to your efforts, no doubt? Oh, and Mr. Dainsleif's, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? What's wrong? You look upset.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon doesn't know the details, either. {NICKNAME} just... disappeared after taking Direidyth's hand... It was like they got sucked into another world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon was looking all over for {M#him}{F#her}... and then {M#he}{F#she} suddenly reappeared, right back in the same spot. But looking a lot more glum.

choices.text: ...It's fine, I just...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: *yawn*...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #I think I got the gist of what happened... Something to do with your {M#sister}{F#brother}? I spoke with the Lord of the Night in a dream just now, and learned quite a lot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh? You met your {M#sister}{F#brother}?

choices.text: I did.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you didn't think to tell Paimon right away!? Well... Never mind. Paimon can see that you're pretty down right now. But let's go over everything later, alright?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #What your {M#sister}{F#brother} accomplished... it all but defies comprehension. I was stunned when I heard about it, too.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But what surprised me the most was that the Lord of the Night actually chose to allow it...

choices.text: That caught me off guard, too.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The Lord of the Night did try to explain it to me, but... in a word, it's complicated.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: During the war with the Abyss, Mavuika had an argument with The Captain.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Mavuika believed that we should fight to protect our culture and memories, while The Captain believed the preservation of the Ley Lines should come before all else.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: So, the Lord of the Night was very intrigued when presented with the Loom of Fate, and informed of its ability to weave Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #She saw your {M#sister}{F#brother}'s actions as a potential third option. Namely, to preserve an entire nation in the form of an "Atlas."

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Preserve a nation...? You've definitely lost me now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... You're not the only one. Paimon's got no idea what's going on either.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: With that in mind, the Lord of the Night gave the go-ahead once she was satisfied that the Loom of Fate wouldn't have any real effect on Natlan.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: However... I believe she imposed an additional condition of her own...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An additional condition? Did she ask for something in return?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No idea. She wouldn't tell me what it was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, well, let's not overthink this for now — we just won a war! Time for a well-earned drink to celebrate.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I trust the Lord of the Night unreservedly. I'm sure she only involved herself to take a problem off our hands. So, it's one less thing for us to worry about.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #Don't you agree, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: You've got a point.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Come on, let's head back to the Collective of Plenty. Varesa should be there, too — we'll treat you to a real feast.

choices.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #Iansan, leave {M#him}{F#her} be.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: This might be hard to understand for an extrovert like you... but some people need alone time to recharge every once in a while.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

choices.text: But there's somewhere else I want to go first.
(I still feel like a mess, though...)
I would never have expected that.
We had a long talk.
I need some time to take everything in.

talks.objective: Return to the cave you were previously in

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before you know it, you've fallen asleep, drowning in a myriad of thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You faintly sense what feels like someone clasping your hand...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But this time, it sends you into a deep sleep, where sweet dreams await.

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: Twilight Sword, Dainsleif... Is this really what you want?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It is indeed. I will take every opportunity to hunt you down to the last man.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, where's {NICKNAME}'s {M#sister}{F#brother}, then? Or is this guy supposed to be in charge here?

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: So, this is a "hunt" to you... I must say, I pity you, Dainsleif. The death you dole out so readily to others is a luxury you yourself cannot enjoy.

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: But today, that is the least of your worries... Do you realize that all your years of pursuing us are being rendered utterly meaningless, even as we speak?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Your riddles tire me. The overwhelming advantage is ours, at least for the moment. You know what that means for you.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I'd like to see what makes you believe you've already won... or that you can still turn the tide of this war.

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: #Then, allow me to be frank. As far as we are concerned... Our {M#Princess}{F#Prince} has already won by other means.

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: #And I do not merely mean this battle. No, {M#Her}{F#His} Highness has achieved something far greater...

dialogues.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
dialogues.text: ...For today, the Abyss Order's greatest wish has finally been fulfilled.

choices.text: The Abyss Order's greatest wish?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Tch...

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: Our Highness quietly infiltrated the Night Kingdom to exploit that realm's past experience with Ley Line reconstruction...

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: And then used the Loom of Fate... to re-weave the Ley Lines of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What!? {M#She}{F#He} used the Loom of Fate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, does this mean the attack on the Masters of the Night-Wind was all a smokescreen to give {M#her}{F#him} some cover?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no... This... makes too much sense...

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: Correct. As of now, our homeland has been revived...

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: And all of my comrades that you have slain, Dainsleif... They shall forget the struggles that have beset them these past five hundred years, and begin their lives anew in a Khaenri'ah restored to life.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: What a load of drivel.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Your falsehoods are riddled with flaws. My ears tire of your tedium.

choices.text: Isn't there more to reviving a homeland...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, you still need a few steps after that... Such as, finding a place to host the Ley Lines you just rewove.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, if it was really so easy, Mavuika and The Captain would have had a way easier time during the war.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: I have one simple question. If Khaenri'ah has indeed been revived as you claim, then where is it?

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: Oh, you poor fools, clinging to delusions even after the truth has been plainly revealed to you...

response.speaker: Iniquitous Baptist
response.text: Think back on the past few days. Have you truly not noticed anything amiss since the start of the war?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Anything amiss... Are there signs that I could have missed?)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I sensed something strange in my dream. It was vague, but... It seemed as if some "noise" had found its way into Natlan's Ley Lines...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does that mean?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hard to say... I don't think it had any tangible effect on the Night Kingdom or on our Ley Lines, but still...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's like... a signal that exists on a different dimension of reality. It might not interfere with ours, or pose any detectable risk, but I just get the sense that something strange is going on.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(I also vaguely remember... seeing {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} in the Night Kingdom, facing the Lord of the Night...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait... That's not all. There were other signs as well...)

choices.text: Than just reweaving its Ley Lines?
Does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What is this... Could this be... The Cataclysm?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is this... Where Direidyth is right now? So, she really is...)

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: We're... not from the same world, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No... I come from your future.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Wait, but that's great! That means the world isn't going to end.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: In that case... Tell me, what happens to Khaenri'ah? What happens to my homeland?

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: No, wait... don't answer that.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: We can only fight for our future if the future is unknown. I still believe the Savior can turn things around.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: #I'll carry on looking for {M#her}{F#him}, even if you're not there to protect me...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Although... In a way...

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: ...I've already found my Savior — it's you. You protected me, and I believe you can protect us all... you're the one who can change everything.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: It's just... too bad that we're not from the same time or place.

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: #Oh, one last thing, before I forget. I know how much you want to find your {M#sister}{F#brother}. Surely, {M#she}{F#he} must be desperate to find you, too?

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: So... Is there anything you can give me as a memento? Proof that we met?

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: #That way, when I do find {M#her}{F#him}, I can convince {M#her}{F#him} that you're also searching for {M#her}{F#him}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A memento...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait...!)

dialogues.speaker: Direidyth
dialogues.text: Huh...? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If this is her future... If this is her fate...)

choices.text: Give the key to <color=#FFCC33FF>Direidyth</color>.
<color=#FFCC33FF>Keep</color> the key.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order retreated when we attacked their stronghold with Iansan and Citlali. This isn't their usual style.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No... that could have been a tactical decision. At least, I can't see how that was directly connected to the revival of Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: According to a guard stationed near the Masters of the Night-Wind, many members of the Abyss Order were seen idling around during the lull in the conflict, even settling down to meditate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait... Could they have been doing that to help the Loom of Fate weave new Ley Lines? But still, that's just a theory, and it also doesn't tell me anything about whether they succeeded.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I couldn't see the monsters that Direidyth could see, and she couldn't see the ones I could. We could only see the monsters in each other's sight after making physical contact.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Direidyth! Great, she's still here.
